   MEMORANDUM

  CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

TO:  Commission Standardization Ad Hoc Committee Liaisons

FROM:  Ryan Gohlich, Assistant City Manager

DATE:  May 28, 2025

SUBJECT:  Review of Arts and Culture Commission Structure and Duties

ATTACHMENTS:  1. February 18, 2025 Commission Standardization Ad Hoc memo

At the Committee’s most recent meeting on February 18, 2025, the Committee discussed duties
and merger opportunities for several commissions. One possible merger that was considered was
the combining of the Recreation and Parks Commission (RPC) with the Arts and Culture
Commission (ACC). While the Committee identified similarities between the RPC and ACC, the
consensus appeared to be that the ACC requires a more specialized skillset when it comes to
selecting fine art installed by the City, as well as evaluating fine art that is installed by private
property owners pursuant to the fine art ordinance. Beyond selecting and evaluating fine art, the
ACC often engages in deep-dive analysis with respect to paint finishes, maintenance and repairs,
placement, and protection (e.g. barriers and landscaping) of fine art pieces, all of which can be
very time intensive outside of the normally scheduled ACC meetings.

In light of the above information, the Committee expressed interest in exploring ways to make the
ACC more efficient such as changing meeting frequency to quarterly instead of monthly, and
having the ACC focus greater attention on fine art instead of events and cultural activities, which
tend to come at the direction of the City Council and often involve overlap with other programming
and commissions. The Committee directed staff do additional work around these topics and return
at a future meeting for further consideration and discussion. Accordingly, this memo focuses on
the ACC and does not recommend any changes to the structure of the RPC at this time.

Arts and Culture Commission Changes for Consideration
Staff has considered the comments provided by the Committee, and has also reviewed the needs
of the Community Services Department to identify areas where the ACC’s work can be most
impactful. As a result, the following recommendations are presented for consideration by the
Committee.

  •  Reduce meeting frequency to quarterly. The Commission currently meets monthly;
  however, a number of the meetings are limited to presentations without substantive
  discussion topics, which may not be the most efficient use of time for Commissioners and
  City resources. Evaluation of fine art issues often takes significant research and time
  outside of regularly scheduled meetings, and it is not uncommon for a specific item of
  discussion to take months of research and analysis before coming back to the
  Commission for discussion. Reducing meeting frequency to quarterly will allow the

  1
   Commission to focus more of its time on substantive items and work efforts outside of the
  regular commission meetings, while also making more efficient use of City resources. In
  the event that an urgent matter comes up for discussion, such as a developer-owned art
  proposal or a special art installation, a special meeting can be called to address the matter
  in a more timely manner.
  •  Rename the Commission to the “Arts Commission” and focus duties around fine,
  visual, and performing arts. Historically, the Commission’s work has focused heavily on
  the fine art ordinance and has only more recently looked at cultural programming, events
  and a broader variety of arts. The City has a need for more focused attention on the
  maintenance of the fine art collection, as well as smaller-scale visual and performing arts
  such as at the Greystone grounds and theater, as well as music and movies at the City’s
  various venues. Focusing the Commission’s attention on these areas will allow for
  improved programming at some of the City’s smaller venues, which tend to be more
  community-serving, without having a significant impact on budget or staffing resources.
  •  Modify or eliminate duties regarding development of new events. The development
  of new events is very resource intensive, both from a staffing and budgetary standpoint,
  and should generally not be undertaken by any commissions without specific City Council
  direction. The City hosts a significant number of events that are already part of the City’s
  budget and ongoing programming. These existing events are managed by Community
  Services staff, and any new events should first be undertaken and directed by the City
  Council so that proper consideration is given to resource constraints and coordination with
  the City’s other events. Ideally, new events should either not overlap with existing City
  events or should be developed in a manner that creates synergies with an existing event
  where the two can be merged together.
  •  Conduct Annual Inspections of Fine Art. The City owns a large collection of fine art,
  and a substantial number of private properties also display fine art in accordance with
  obligations in the fine art ordinance. As the collection of fine art continues to grow, there
  is a greater and greater need to track, document, and ensure the appropriate maintenance
  of fine art throughout the City. In years past the Commission has undertaken field work to
  inspect and document existing fine art. This work effort was quite valuable, as it allowed
  the City to maintain up-to-date records regarding the location and condition of fine art to
  ensure that required art remains in place, and that it is maintained in a manner that
  provides an ongoing benefit to the greater community. Accordingly, staff recommends
  establishing annual fine art inspections as a primary duty of the Commission. If
  Commission meetings are adjusted to a quarterly schedule, the additional time between
  meetings can be used for field work associated with annual inspections, and each year
  the Community Services Department will be able to produce a report highlighting the
  status of fine art throughout the City. This information will enhance documentation and
  can also be used to create greater variety in art walks.

Recommendation
This report is intended as a high-level overview of ways in which the structure and duties of the
ACC can be modified to be more efficient, while at the same time providing enhanced value to
the community by focusing more strategically on local-serving activities. Depending on the
direction provided by the Committee, staff would plan to draft detailed ordinance changes that are
reflective of the items above or any other direction provided by the Committee, and said ordinance
could either be brought back to the Committee or taken directly to the full City Council.

Standardization Ad Hoc Memo
   MEMORANDUM

  CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

TO:  Commission Standardization Ad Hoc Committee Liaisons

FROM:  Ryan Gohlich, Assistant City Manager

DATE:  February 18, 2025

SUBJECT:  Commission Merger Opportunities to Streamline Operations

ATTACHMENTS:  1. Commission Duties

Since the establishment of the Commission Standardization Ad Hoc Committee, the Committee
has met multiple times to discuss opportunities for standardization and streamlining of the City’s
various commissions. Through these efforts, the Committee has made recommendations to
consolidate and/or eliminate commissions where appropriate, and has also made
recommendations to clarify a number of policies applicable to the recruitment of new
commissioners as vacancies become available. At the Committee’s most recent meeting in
November 2024, the Committee reviewed the duties of the Health and Safety Commission (HSC),
Human Relations Commission (HRC), Recreation and Parks Commission (RPC), and Arts and
Culture Commission (ACC). The Committee heard an initial report regarding potential overlap of
commission duties, and considered whether there were synergies between the commissions that
might warrant a merger of the HSC with the HRC, and a merger of the RPC with the ACC.

During the meeting, several current commissioners voiced concerns that proper consideration
was not being given to the work of each commission, and that although there may be some
overlap, there are distinct duties for each commission that involve some level of expertise in a
given field that may not be conducive to mergers. After taking public comment on the matter, the
Committee directed staff to further analyze the work of each commission, what goes into
supporting each commission, and to provide increased notice to commissioners prior to the next
meeting in order to allow for additional perspectives and analysis.

In response to the Committee’s direction, staff has reviewed commission agendas over the last
several years to help identify similarities and differences between the commissions to better
inform the discussion and identify the degree to which there may be overlap between
commissions. In addition, staff has reviewed the level of staff support and resources that are
typically associated with the commissions in question. The following sections in this report discuss
staff’s findings relative to the Committee’s direction.

Health and Safety Commission / Human Relations Commission
The HSC and HRC both meet monthly, with the HSC being supported by the Fire Department
and the HRC being supported by the Community Services Department. The prior report to the
Committee regarding the work of the two commissions highlighted the duties of each commission
as described in the municipal code; however, this report looks more closely at the topics discussed

  1
 at each of the commissions’ meetings over the past several years to identify similarities and
differences. The following list is not intended to be exhaustive of every single agenda item, but is
intended to highlight themes (often recurring), as well as specific programs worked on or
discussed by the commissions.

  Topics of Discussion Common to Both the HSC and HRC

  •  Monthly reports from BHPD and BHUSD
  •  Day of Wellness
  •  National Night Out
  •  Learning about and addressing hate crime
  •  Unhoused issues and City's related responses/programs
  •  Mental health and wellbeing
  •  Bullying and social media
  •  Safety-related discussions
  •  Community Assistance Grant Funding

  Topics of Discussion Unique to the HSC

  •  Monthly reports from BHFD
  •  Smoking
  •  COVID
  •  Water quality and supply
  •  Emergency preparedness
  •  Chronic illnesses

  Topics of Discussion Unique to the HRC

  •  Civility programs
  •  Beverly Hills Reads
  •  Kindness Matters
  •  Critical Conversations

  While there do appear to be topics that are unique to each commission, on balance there
  appear to be more similarities than differences between the topics covered by each
  commission. Moreover, the general theme of items routinely discussed by both commissions
  appears to revolve around health, community education, wellness, and safety. The Committee
  should take this into consideration when weighing whether merger of the commissions would
  streamline operations and prevent overlap of duties and topics. If there is interest in merging

  2
   the commissions, staff recommends maintaining, but consolidating, the major duties of the
  commissions in order to provide a consistent level of value and service to the City Council and
  community. As in the past, staff would also recommend timing any merger in coordination with
  natural attrition of commissioners so as not to reduce the terms of any sitting commissioners.
  If so directed, staff will develop merged duties and timelines to be presented to the full City
  Council.

Recreation and Parks Commission / Arts and Culture Commission
The RPC and ACC both meet monthly, and both commissions are supported by the Community
Services Department. The prior report to the Committee regarding the work of the two
commissions highlighted the duties of each commission as described in the municipal code;
however, this report looks more closely at the topics discussed at each of the commissions’
meetings over the past several years to identify similarities and differences. The following list is
not intended to be exhaustive of every single agenda item, but is intended to highlight themes
(often recurring), as well as specific programs worked on by the commissions.

  Topics of Discussion Common to Both the RPC and ACC

  •  Greystone events and programming
  •  Farmers Market events
  •  Festival Beverly Hills
  •  Beverly Hills Art Show
  •  Wellness and kindness
  •  Concerts on Canon

  Topics of Discussion Unique to the RPC

  •  Park projects and renovations
  •  Park programing and rules
  •  Pickleball
  •  BHUSD updates
  •  Senior programming and events
  •  Library and reading programs
  •  Youth and teen programming

  Topics of Discussion Unique to the ACC

  •  Fine Art approval, acquisition, maintenance, and funding
  •  Art and artist resources
  •  Cultural/social recognitions
  •  Artwalks

  3
   •  Make Music Day

  As with the earlier analysis concerning the HSC and HRC, both the RPC and ACC do appear
  to cover topics that are unique to each commission; however, there are an almost equal
  amount of similar topics or projects where there appears to be overlap between the two
  commissions. The vast majority of public events, cultural or otherwise, tend to occur in the
  City’s parks, which is likely a significant cause for overlap between the commissions. The
  primary differences between the commissions tend to be predominantly driven by fine art (or
  art in general), as well as day-to-day services offered at the City’s parks as opposed to event
  programming, which tends to overlap between the commissions. The common denominator
  between the two commissions seems to be use of the City’s parks, and the parks are often a
  central component (e.g. placement of art) even when there is not an overlap of duties. The
  Committee should take this into consideration when weighing whether merger of the
  commissions would streamline operations and prevent overlap of duties and topics, which
  seems to be a reasonable path forward given the similarities.

  Although it appears that all relevant duties could be absorbed by a single commission, in the
  event that there is a desire to maintain some specialized knowledge for fine art, another
  alternative to consider would be to shift all duties to the RPC since parks are a focal point, but
  revert the ACC back to the former Fine Art Commission. Under this scenario, a Fine Art
  Commission could meet quarterly instead of monthly, with a focus strictly on fine art.

  If there is interest in merging the commissions, staff recommends maintaining, but
  consolidating, the major duties of the commissions in order to provide a consistent level of
  value and service to the City Council and community. In addition, there should be a
  requirement that at least one or two commissioners have a background in the art field in order
  to maintain technical expertise for review of art. As in the past, staff would also recommend
  timing any merger in coordination with natural attrition of commissioners so as not to reduce
  the terms of any sitting commissioners.

Resource Utilization
Beyond simply comparing the work of each commission to determine what degree of overlap may
exist, the Committee should also consider the level of resources required to support each
commission. To many, operating a commission may seem like a somewhat simple undertaking
with limited resource needs for a single meeting per month, but there is in fact a substantial
amount of staff time (and budget) that is required to effectively support a commission. Staff time
spent supporting a commission typically includes:

  •  Creation of agendas
  •  Drafting and review of reports
  •  Coordinating with other departments
  •  Digitizing of agenda packets
  •  Printing of agenda packets (often 15 or more copies)
  •  Delivery of agenda packets to commissioner homes or businesses
  •  Online publication of agenda packets
  •  Physical posting of agendas
  •  Placement of physical agenda packets in public places
  •  Pre-meetings with commissioners
  •  Preparation of presentations
  •  Setup and teardown of commission meeting room

  4
   •  Recording and broadcasting of meeting (typically at least two cable TV staff)
  •  Editing and online uploading of completed meetings
  •  Attendance by staff at commission meetings (typically four or five department staff)
  •  Attendance by other departments or agencies (BHPD, BHFD, BHUSD, PW, etc.)
  •  Preparation and distribution of meeting minutes
  •  Commissioner training
  •  Engaging with stakeholders and interested parties outside of the public meeting
  •  Coordinating guest speakers and preparing them for the meeting
  •  Coordinating ad-hoc/standing committee and liaison meetings
  •  Preparation for and attendance at ad-hoc/standing committee and liaison meetings
  •  Advancing initiatives to the full City Council

While the above list is not necessarily exhaustive, it is intended to demonstrate the time-intensive
work that goes on behind the scenes in preparation for almost every single meeting. Although the
workload for each commission meeting will vary based on the number and complexity of agenda
items, it is not uncommon to spend between 100 and 200 staff hours on a single meeting that
typically lasts for two to four hours.

In terms of dollars, the cost of supporting a single commission easily runs into the hundreds of
thousands of dollars annually, and perhaps of equal or greater importance, results in the
opportunity cost of staff time being focused on commission support instead of ongoing services
and programs.

Recommendation
As part of the City’s ongoing efforts to streamline commission work, inclusive of reducing actual
costs and reallocating resources associated with staffing and supporting commission meetings
and activities, staff seeks recommendations from the Committee regarding the following:

  1. Should the HSC be merged with the HRC?

  2. Should the RPC be merged with the ACC, or should a hybrid that restores the Fine Art
  Commission be pursued?

Staff’s analysis generally concludes that there is significant overlap of like topics among the
commissions as discussed in this report, and that mergers are a feasible means of streamlining
operations without diminishing the value provided by each commission. Depending on the
direction received, staff would plan to present recommendations to the full City Council regarding
any mergers, necessary code changes regarding consolidation of duties, as well as a timeline to
complete the mergers in a manner that does not reduce the terms of any sitting commissioners.

Commission Duties
 Health and Safety Commission
The health and safety commission shall strive to maintain and improve the overall health and
safety of the community in accordance with its purposes and responsibilities. The commission
shall have the following purposes and responsibilities:

  1. Increase Public Awareness: Promote and broaden community awareness of health
  and safety issues, including issues of public health and welfare, healthy lifestyles,
  mitigation of safety risks and hazards, the importance of disaster preparedness
  (hereafter "health and safety issues") and encourage citizen participation in efforts
  aimed at promoting health and safety issues.
  2. Inform The Public: Educate and inform members of the community regarding health
  and safety issues and risk avoidance through various means, including, but not limiting
  to, public discussion, website publications and postings, community outreach, sharing
  of information and by assisting at and supporting city sponsored activities and
  programs which promote health and safety issues.
  3. Provide A Public Forum: Provide the community with a public forum within which
  members of the general public can discuss and/or comment on health and safety
  issues.
  4. Provide Recommendations: Recommend strategies aimed at improving the health and
  safety of the city, including as directed by the city council, or as requested by members
  of the general public, and/or which relate to health and safety issues.
  5. Support Efforts Aimed At Disaster Preparedness, Prevention, Mitigation, Response
  And Recovery: Support the work of all city departments before, during and after a
  medical, natural or manmade disaster, and strengthen ties with the community's
  disaster related stakeholders.
  6. Recognize Achievement: Honor individuals, businesses or groups that have
  demonstrated leadership in the field of health and safety, have promoted health and
  safety issues and/or have otherwise made a contribution to the missions of the health
  and safety commission.

Human Relations Commission
The human relations commission shall advise, recommend, assist and encourage activities
and programs to be undertaken to promote positive human relations in all aspects of
community life in Beverly Hills. The commission shall actively promote a just and equitable
multicultural society; and will endeavor to reduce conflict and tension, as well as
discrimination, prejudice and stereotyping based on race, religion, gender, sexual orientation,
national origin, age, disability, or any other arbitrary factor.

The purposes and responsibilities of the commission shall include:

  A. Promoting the concepts of diversity, tolerance, and acceptance in the community;
  B. Conducting such studies and to hear such issues in any field of human relations in the
  community as will aid in effectuating the commission's general purpose;
  C. Inquiring into incidents of tension or conflict among or between various racial, religious
  or nationality groups, and encouraging action by means of conciliation, conference,
  and/or persuasion to alleviate such tensions and conflict;
   D. Conducting and/or recommending such educational programs as will increase good
  will throughout the community;
  E. Defining, identifying and tracking existing and emerging issues that may benefit from
  intervention or conflict resolution;
  F. Facilitating better communication and interpersonal relations within the city and
  between the city and members of the community and hearing and receiving oral and
  written communications, in an appropriate time and manner, from members of the
  public concerning any topic that relates to the relationships between members of the
  community or between the city or its staff and members of the community;
  G. Receiving citizen complaints, in an appropriate time and manner, concerning the
  interactions of city employees with the public. The commission shall serve as one
  alternative to directing complaints to the city department involved in the complaint.
  1. The commission or its staff may communicate with complainants and city
  departments with regard to complaints received by the commission and may also
  arrange and facilitate communications directly between city departments and
  complainants;
  2. The commission or its staff may inquire about the status of a complaint received
  by the commission and the progress of the review of a complaint;
  H. Landlord-Tenant Issues:
  1. The commission shall hear landlord-tenant disputes in order to provide a public
  forum where tenants and landlords can address issues and resolve differences
  prior to pursuing mediation, requesting a formal hearing with the city, if applicable,
  or filing a civil suit.
  2. The commission shall educate tenants in the City regarding tenant rights.

Recreation and Parks Commission
The Recreation and Parks Commission shall perform the following functions:
  A. Act as an advisory body to the City Council on matters which relate to recreation and
  parks programs and facilities, including, without limitation, the Greystone estate
  grounds and mansion.
  B. Advise and make recommendations to the Director of Recreation and Parks, or his
  designee, on the planning, evaluation and delivery of recreation and parks programs
  and facilities including:
  1. Formulating general policies on use and delivery of recreation and park services;
  2. Evaluating the effectiveness of programs in relation to City Council policy
  objectives;
  3. Assisting in communications with the community concerning recreation and parks
  programs.
  C. Advise the City Council and staff regarding capital improvements and program projects
  for recreation and parks improvements.
  D. Provide recommendations on proposed user fees for use of recreation and parks
  facilities and programs.
   E. Perform such other duties relating to recreation and parks matters as may be referred
  to it by the City Council, or the Director of Recreation and Parks, or his representative.

  Arts and Culture Commission
  The mission of the Arts and Culture Commission is to promote and nurture the arts and cultural
  life of the City of Beverly Hills.
  The Arts and Culture Commission shall have the following powers and duties:
  A. Act in an advisory capacity to the City Council on matters pertaining to the enrichment
  of the community through fine arts, visual arts, performing arts, digital and media arts,
  arts education, and community cultural activities, education and events;
  B. Serve as an advocate for cultural activities, community cultural programs and events
  within the City;
  C. Promote arts and culture activities of and in the City to broaden the opportunities for
  residents and visitors' participation in the arts;
  D. Implement the City's Fine Art Program, as specified in sections 3-1-801 through 3-1-
  814 of this Code, including, but not limited to, the purchase of fine art for the public,
  consideration of donations and loans of public art, hosting art exhibits or art events,
  and performance of such other duties relating to procurement, display and
  maintenance of fine art as designated by the City Council;
  E. Foster public and private partnerships for providing arts and cultural programming,
  including enhancing and expanding community cultural events by involving artists, art
  galleries, fine and visual arts, performing arts, digital and media arts, literary arts and
  creative arts organizations, the creative community, residents and the business
  community;
  F. Promote access to the highest quality arts and cultural opportunities possible;
  G. Encourage the integration of cultural programs and community cultural events into
  fabric of the City to improve the quality of life for City residents and welcome visitors
  to the world-class Beverly Hills experience;
  H. Encourage and support arts education programs in the community and schools
  including docent programs or similar;
Perform such other duties, not inconsistent with this Code, as may be prescribed by ordinance,
resolution, City Council policy or other City Council action.
